questions.question: What is the net horizontal force on the box?
questions.feedback: Equal and opposite forces cancel.

image.alt: A box has a 10 N arrow pointing left and a 10 N arrow pointing right.

questions.question: What is the net horizontal force on the box?
questions.feedback: Subtract opposing forces and keep the direction of the larger force.

image.alt: A box has a 6 N arrow pointing left and a 10 N arrow pointing right.

questions.question: Which way does gravity act on this ball after it leaves the thrower’s hand?
options: Along the ball’s direction of travel
questions.feedback: Gravity acts towards Earth throughout the flight.

image.alt: A ball is in the air after being released.

questions.question: The box is sliding to the right along a stationary bench. Which way does friction from the bench act on the box?
questions.feedback: Friction opposes the sliding between the box and bench.

image.alt: A right-pointing arrow shows the box moving to the right.

questions.question: What upward force does the table exert on the resting book?
questions.feedback: The table pushes upwards on the book with a support force.

image.alt: A book rests on the flat top of a table.

questions.question: Which example involves a contact force?
options: A magnet attracting a paperclip without touching it
A charged balloon attracting hair across a gap
questions.feedback: The foot must touch the ball to kick it.

questions.question: Which quantity is measured in newtons?
questions.feedback: Weight is a force. Mass is measured in kilograms.

questions.question: A cyclist travels in a straight line at a constant speed. What is the net force on the cyclist and bike?
questions.feedback: Constant speed in a straight line means the forces balance.

questions.question: Why does a parachute slow a falling skydiver when it opens?
options: It reduces the mass of the skydiver
It pulls the skydiver down faster
questions.feedback: The open parachute increases the upward force from air resistance.

questions.question: Two students push a trolley in the same direction with forces of 12 N and 8 N. What is the combined force of their pushes?
questions.feedback: Forces in the same direction add together.

questions.question: What is a force?
options: The amount of matter in an object
questions.feedback: Forces are pushes or pulls.

questions.question: Which tool measures the size of a force?
questions.feedback: A spring balance can measure force in newtons.

questions.question: What force pulls a dropped pencil towards the floor?
questions.feedback: Earth’s gravity pulls the pencil downward.

questions.question: What is mass a measure of?
options: The amount of matter in an object
questions.answer: The amount of matter in an object
questions.feedback: Mass measures the amount of matter.

questions.question: Which surface usually provides the most grip for a shoe?
questions.feedback: A dry rough surface usually provides more friction.

questions.question: Which force opposes movement through air?
questions.feedback: Air resistance acts against motion relative to the air.

questions.question: Which object pulls on an iron paperclip across a gap?
options: A ruler made of plain wood
questions.feedback: A magnet can attract iron without touching it.

questions.question: What does the arrowhead in a force diagram show?
questions.feedback: Force arrows point in the direction the force acts.

questions.question: On a force diagram using one scale, what does a longer arrow show?
options: A heavier object in every case
questions.feedback: Arrow length represents force magnitude.

questions.question: Which force helps a bicycle brake slow the wheel?
questions.feedback: Friction at the brake opposes rotation.

questions.question: What can an unbalanced force change?
options: The unit used to measure it
questions.feedback: A net force changes motion.

questions.question: Which is a non-contact force?
options: Gravity between Earth and the Moon
questions.answer: Gravity between Earth and the Moon
questions.feedback: Gravity acts across a distance.

questions.question: A rope is pulled left with 18 N and right with 11 N. What is the net force?
questions.feedback: The leftward force exceeds the rightward force by 7 N.

questions.question: A puck is moving left. A net force acts to the right. What happens at first?
options: It speeds up to the left.
questions.feedback: A force opposite the motion initially reduces speed.

questions.question: A toy car starts moving from rest. What does that tell you about its forces?
options: They were unbalanced while it started moving.
questions.answer: They were unbalanced while it started moving.
questions.feedback: Starting from rest involves a change in velocity.

questions.question: An astronaut travels from Earth to the Moon. What happens?
options: Mass stays the same and weight decreases.
Mass and weight both stay the same.
Mass decreases and weight stays the same.
questions.answer: Mass stays the same and weight decreases.
questions.feedback: The Moon’s weaker gravity reduces weight without changing mass.

questions.question: Why do people put oil on a bicycle chain?
options: To reduce friction between moving parts
To stop the wheels from turning
questions.answer: To reduce friction between moving parts
questions.feedback: Lubrication reduces friction and wear.

questions.question: What force moves a swimmer forward when they push water backwards?
options: The forward push of the water on the swimmer
The backward push of the swimmer on the water
questions.answer: The forward push of the water on the swimmer
questions.feedback: The water pushes back on the swimmer.

questions.question: A lift moves upward at constant velocity. How do its upward and downward forces compare?
questions.feedback: Constant velocity requires zero net force.

questions.question: A floating leaf drifts steadily downstream. Which force keeps it from sinking?
options: An upward push from the water
questions.answer: An upward push from the water
questions.feedback: Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by the water.

questions.question: A stretched elastic band is pulling on two hooks. What happens if one hook is released?
options: The band tends to return towards its unstretched length.
The band keeps pulling on the released hook at a distance.
The band’s elastic force reverses gravity.
questions.answer: The band tends to return towards its unstretched length.
questions.feedback: Elastic forces tend to restore the original shape.

questions.question: A tray is at rest. Gravity pulls down with 15 N. If the table is the only other force, what does it exert?
questions.feedback: The support force balances the weight.

questions.question: Why do wide tyres with deep tread help on a muddy track?
options: They can improve grip with the ground.
They make the vehicle’s weight zero.
questions.answer: They can improve grip with the ground.
questions.feedback: Tread can help the tyres push against soft ground.

questions.question: What should stay the same when comparing how surface type affects a block’s sliding friction?
options: The block and how it is pulled
The force reading for each trial
questions.answer: The block and how it is pulled
questions.feedback: Keeping other variables constant isolates the effect of surface type.

questions.question: Ignoring air resistance, why would different-mass balls dropped together reach the floor together?
options: Gravity gives both the same acceleration at that location.
Both have exactly the same weight.
The larger ball experiences no gravity.
The smaller ball falls only after the larger one lands.
questions.answer: Gravity gives both the same acceleration at that location.
questions.feedback: The larger gravitational force on a heavier mass produces the same acceleration.

questions.question: Which pair shows equal and opposite forces acting on different objects?
options: A bat pushes a ball and the ball pushes the bat.
Gravity pulls a book down and a table pushes it up.
Two students push the same trolley in opposite directions.
Weight and air resistance act on the same falling leaf.
questions.answer: A bat pushes a ball and the ball pushes the bat.
questions.feedback: Interaction pairs act on different objects.

questions.question: A car turns a corner at constant speed. Why is its net force not zero?
options: Its wheels always point straight ahead.
questions.feedback: A direction change is a change in velocity.

questions.question: A balloon moves towards a wall after being rubbed. If it moves before contact, what force is responsible?
questions.feedback: Electric charges can attract across a gap.

questions.question: A cart has 20 N forward thrust and 7 N friction. How much extra backward force would balance it?
questions.feedback: The current net force is 13 N forward.

questions.question: A box has 12 N left, 5 N right and another 3 N right. What is the net force?
questions.feedback: Rightward forces total 8 N, leaving 4 N left.

questions.question: A moving skateboard has zero net force. What happens on a straight level track?
options: It continues with the same speed and direction.
questions.answer: It continues with the same speed and direction.
questions.feedback: Zero net force means no change in velocity.

questions.question: A spring scale reads 9 N to start a block sliding and 6 N to keep it moving steadily. What does this suggest?
options: Starting motion required a larger pull than maintaining steady sliding.
Friction was larger after the block started sliding.
The block lost 3 N of weight.
The scale measured the block’s speed.
questions.answer: Starting motion required a larger pull than maintaining steady sliding.
questions.feedback: The readings compare the pull needed before and during sliding.

questions.question: A dropped object reaches terminal speed. What does this tell us about the forces?
options: Its weight must be less than air resistance.
questions.feedback: At constant falling speed the upward and downward forces balance.

questions.question: A rover weighs 120 N on Earth. On a planet with half Earth’s gravitational field strength, what would it weigh?
questions.feedback: With unchanged mass, weight halves when field strength halves.

questions.question: One cart has double the mass of another. Both experience the same net force. Which speeds up faster?
options: Both speed up at the same rate.
questions.feedback: The same net force produces greater acceleration on a smaller mass.

questions.question: A student pulls a block faster on carpet than on tile. Why is this a weak comparison of the surfaces?
options: Pulling speed and surface both changed.
The blocks were the same size.
They used the same measuring tool.
questions.answer: Pulling speed and surface both changed.
questions.feedback: Changing two variables makes it harder to attribute any difference to the surface.

questions.question: A ball rolls right up a ramp and slows. What can you infer about its net force along the ramp?
options: It has a component down the ramp.
It has a component up the ramp.
It is zero while the ball is moving.
It points right and gets larger.
questions.answer: It has a component down the ramp.
questions.feedback: The velocity changes down the ramp as the ball slows.

questions.question: Two magnets repel with a gap between them. How do their forces on each other compare?
options: Equal in size and opposite in direction
The larger magnet always exerts more force.
Only the moving magnet experiences force.
Both forces point in the same direction.
questions.answer: Equal in size and opposite in direction
questions.feedback: Each magnet exerts an equal and opposite force on the other.

questions.question: A student says still objects have no forces on them. Which evidence best challenges that idea?
options: A motionless hanging mass stretches a spring.
A ball rolls down a slope.
A cart speeds up when pushed.
questions.answer: A motionless hanging mass stretches a spring.
questions.feedback: A stretched spring reveals an upward force balancing the hanging mass’s weight.

questions.question: Why doesn’t a boat necessarily speed up when its motor is on?
options: Water resistance can balance the forward thrust.
The boat’s mass always increases when the motor starts.
questions.answer: Water resistance can balance the forward thrust.
questions.feedback: Balanced forces let the boat travel at constant velocity.
